title: Entering cybersecurity after a CS degree
samplePrompt: I'm majoring in CS and want to work in cybersecurity. What if AI changes the entry-level jobs?

followUp.question: Which work are you aiming for?

options.label: Security operations center (SOC) analyst who reviews alerts

followUp.unsupportedNote: This scenario models a SOC analyst role. Choose that role to continue.

riskSummary: Pay you could miss while waiting to start a cybersecurity job.

inputs.name: extraMonths
inputs.label: Extra months until first paid work

company.name: Palo Alto Networks
company.fact: Its Cortex XSIAM product automates parts of security operations, and the company describes analysts using it for alert handling and investigations.
company.caveat: Those facts also support a competing explanation: a team could adopt the tool and keep its junior analysts. The career outcome and the investment outcome each need their own assumption.

scenarios.label: Employers automate some junior work and the vendor gains customers
scenarios.reason: Adoption of the vendor's automation platform grows revenue faster than the hiring slowdown hurts it.

scenarios.label: A spending freeze slows both hiring and software sales
scenarios.reason: The same macro slowdown that delays hiring also cuts the vendor's sales — the stock falls with the risk.

scenarios.label: Analysts use the tool and hiring stays on schedule
scenarios.reason: Teams augment analysts instead of replacing them — the feared exposure never materializes.

title: Buying a gas car for commuting
samplePrompt: I'm buying a gas car for my commute. Can an energy stock cushion a fuel-price spike?

followUp.question: How many miles will you drive this year, and what mileage does the car get?

riskSummary: Extra dollars spent at the pump if fuel averages above the budgeted price.

company.name: Valero
company.fact: Its refining margin depends on the prices of the products it sells and the inputs it buys.
company.caveat: A commuter's pump price also includes taxes, distribution, and retail costs. A price increase caused by a local charge can affect the driver without improving the refiner's margin.

scenarios.label: Fuel supply tightens and the refiner's margins expand
scenarios.reason: Tighter product supply widens refining margins, so the refiner's stock rises with the driver's fuel costs.

scenarios.label: A local charge raises the same pump price and the stock ends flat
scenarios.reason: Taxes and local charges raise the pump price without touching refining margins — the driver pays more but the refiner gains nothing.

title: Tuition billed in yen for a semester in Japan
samplePrompt: I'm committing to a semester in Japan. What if the yen rises before tuition is due?

followUp.question: Is the bill fixed in yen or in US dollars?

period: Six months until tuition is due
riskSummary: Change in the dollar cost of a future yen bill if the exchange rate moves.

fixedMode.message: Your tuition is already fixed in dollars — there is no currency exposure to hedge.
fixedMode.note: Cash held in yen can still change value. This example assumes no conversion fees or interest.

company.name: Toyota
company.fact: Its filing explains how exchange rates affect its global business.
company.caveat: Owning a Japanese business is not the same as owning the currency you will owe — compare against holding yen directly.

sources.label: Toyota annual filing, foreign currency fluctuations

scenarios.label: Yen strengthens and Toyota shares fall in dollar terms
scenarios.reason: A stronger yen squeezes an exporter's overseas earnings when converted back — the stock falls in USD terms.

scenarios.label: Same currency move and strong vehicle sales lift the shares
scenarios.reason: Vehicle demand outweighs the currency drag — the stock rises even as the yen bill grows.

scenarios.label: Convert $1,000 to yen now and hold until tuition is due
scenarios.reason: Directly holding the currency you owe removes the mismatch — the gain is calculated from the two exchange rates, not assumed.
